notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.29_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.29.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.29.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **Linking a device shows you it filling up.** Taking on an account is quick
  — a key, a name, a list of servers — and what takes time is the documents
  behind them arriving from whichever of your devices and friends happen to be
  awake. In between sat a device that looked finished and had nothing in it,
  which is indistinguishable from one where something went wrong. Now it says
  which it is: the servers and friends that came with the account, then a
  count of what has actually landed, naming whatever it is still waiting for.

  You can leave at any point — what has not arrived goes on arriving. It shows
  on the first-run screen as well as in account settings, which is where a new
  phone actually goes, and that screen now waits for you rather than dropping
  you into an empty sidebar the moment the account is adopted.

- **Ruze keeps a log, and can be asked for a detailed one.** The whole
  peer-to-peer half of the app has always reported what it was doing —
  connections, syncing, voice, pairing — to nowhere at all: there was no
  subscriber listening, in any build. So a call that hung or a server that
  quietly stopped updating left nothing behind to look at, and the only way
  to investigate was to be sitting at the machine it happened on.

  Now there is a file per run, kept for the last eight runs, and a switch that
  turns the network layer's own reporting on with it. It is behind seven taps
  on the "Settings" heading, because it is not a setting anybody should be
  choosing between — it is there for when somebody is being talked through
  getting a log out. Nothing anybody typed and no key of any kind is ever
  written to it, and the panel says plainly what *is* in it before offering to
  copy it.

### Changed

- **Linking an existing account asks first, and replaces rather than
  merges.** It is the most destructive button in account settings — the
  account already on the device stops being it — and it was the one route
  that did it the instant it was pressed, while the two slower ones both
  warned you. Now all three go through the same warning, which names the
  account being replaced. Scanning a code goes through it too; a camera can
  read the wrong one.

  What it does afterwards has changed. Linking used to leave the old
  account's servers and friends in place and add the new account's on top, so
  a phone ended up showing both at once — and it announced the account you
  had just linked as a member of servers only the old identity had ever
  joined. Now the device ends up with what the account you linked to has, and
  the warning offers a tick box to bring the old one's servers and friends
  across instead, for folding an old identity into the one you actually use.
  Either way nothing is deleted: the old account keeps everything wherever
  its phrase still is.

### Fixed

- **Android no longer opens on a desktop window frame.** Launching the app
  drew the desktop title bar — with the window controls a phone has no use
  for — and then replaced it with the real thing a moment later. Ruze asked
  the backend which platform it was on and assumed desktop until the answer
  came back, and that question was the eleventh in a queue of them, so the
  wrong frame sat there for the whole of startup rather than for an instant.
  The platform is now known before anything is drawn.

- **A microphone that will not open no longer freezes Ruze.** Joining a voice
  channel opens your microphone and speakers first, and asking the operating
  system for a device is a wait it decides the length of — a Bluetooth headset
  still listed as the default after it has gone, a device asleep since the
  machine was, another application holding it. Ruze waited for that with no
  limit at all, on a thread it needed for everything else, so a device that
  never answered left the window on "Connecting…" and the rest of the app
  stopped with it.

  Now the wait is bounded and happens out of the way: twelve seconds, and then
  it says the device did not respond and suggests checking it. The same fault
  was in the microphone test and the speaker test tone, and all three are
  fixed together.

- **Your other devices' messages reach this one.** Two devices signed into the
  same account never exchanged the half of a conversation they both write:
  it lives in a document derived from your account key, so nothing hands it
  over and neither device had anywhere to start looking for the other. They
  each kept their own copy of the same conversation, indefinitely. Devices now
  learn about each other when an account is handed over, and from the account's
  own card after that.

- **A message from your own other device is recognised as yours.** It carries
  the id of the device that wrote it, and anything not written *here* was
  treated as somebody else's — so a message sent from your desktop arrived on
  your phone drawn on the wrong side, chiming, counted as unread, and in a
  conversation it wore the other person's name and picture, because in a
  conversation there is only one other person it could be. Reactions had the
  same problem, and one you left on another device now says "You".

- **A server or conversation that could not reach anyone the first time gets
  the next chance.** Once something was syncing, a later attempt carrying
  better addresses — a fresh invite, a device that has just appeared — was
  dropped rather than passed on, so it went the rest of the session looking in
  the places that had not worked.
